title: Blob SAS and User Delegation SAS
description: Learn how to grant limited, time-bound access to blobs using Shared Access Signatures and user delegation SAS tokens.

data.text: A **Shared Access Signature (SAS)** is a URI that grants restricted access to a storage resource without exposing your account key. You control what the client can do (read, write, delete), what resources they can reach, and how long the permission lasts. A **user delegation SAS** is signed with Azure AD credentials instead of an account key, giving even tighter control.

data.title: SAS Types
items: **User delegation SAS** — signed by a user or managed identity using Azure AD. Recommended for production because it does not expose account keys.
**Service SAS** — signed with an account key and scoped to a specific service, like Blob or Queue.
**Account SAS** — signed with an account key and grants access to multiple services. Use only when absolutely necessary.

data.text: A SAS token is a query string appended to a URL. Each parameter restricts a specific aspect of access. Understanding the parameters helps you build the minimum-permission token your application needs.

rows: Permissions: r=read, w=write, c=create, d=delete, l=list, a=add, u=update, p=process
Signature — HMAC hash of the token string

data.title: Generate a SAS with Azure CLI
data.content: Create a service SAS for read access to a single blob
data.code:
az storage blob generate-sas \
  --account-name stdemostorage \
  --container-name uploads \
  --name photo.jpg \
  --permissions r \
  --expiry 2025-12-31T23:59Z \
  --https-only \
  --output tsv

terms.definition: A URI that grants restricted access to a storage resource using signed query parameters.
A SAS signed by an Azure AD identity rather than a storage account key, providing better security and auditability.
A reusable policy on a container that defines SAS constraints, allowing you to revoke or modify a SAS without changing the token itself.

data.title: Never Expose Account Keys
data.text: Account keys grant full access to your storage account. Use user delegation SAS in production and never embed keys in client-side code, mobile apps, or public repositories.

data.title: Exercise: Generate and Use a SAS
data.description: Create a read-only SAS for a blob and download it using the SAS URL.
steps: Upload a text file to your container.
Generate a read-only SAS that expires in 30 minutes using Azure CLI.
Copy the resulting URL into a browser or curl command.
Try to write to the blob using the same SAS URL and confirm it is blocked.
data.expectedOutcome: A working read-only SAS URL that allows download but prevents write operations.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SAS tokens grant limited, time-bound access without exposing account keys.
User delegation SAS is the most secure option because it uses Azure AD.
Always set the minimum required permissions and shortest practical expiry.
Use stored access policies when you need to revoke a SAS before it expires.
data.takeaway: SAS tokens let you share storage resources safely. Next, you will use them from actual applications.
